lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: restricting a domain so an inverse can be constructed
lessonRef.title: Investigation or close reading: restricting a domain so an inverse can be constructed

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example shows the kind of reasoning the investigation asks for.

steps: Which angle in [−π/2, π/2] has sine 1/2?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what changes and what stays fixed before you answer.

items.prompt: Why does cosine on all real numbers not have an inverse function without further restriction?
choices: Because its outputs are not all positive.
It repeats with period π, so the domain is restricted to (−π/2, π/2) to make an inverse possible.
It is not one-to-one — infinitely many inputs give the same output — so it has no inverse until the domain is restricted to [−π/2, π/2].
It is not one-to-one, so the domain is restricted to [0, π] to make an inverse possible.

sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Write out the reasoning in full sentences. A correct answer with no justification does not count here.
